title: Open Problem: Characterization of parameters satisfying (CC)
statement_text: Characterize the (hereditary, connected) graph parameters $f$ satisfying property (CC): for all integers $p$ and $s$, there exist two integers $p'$ and $s'$ such that $\mathrm{col}_{f,p'}(G) \leq s'$ for every graph $G$ satisfying $\chi^\ell_{f,p}(G) \leq s$.
context_text: A graph parameter $f$ assigns to every graph a value in $\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\}$, equal on isomorphic graphs; it is hereditary if $f(H)\le f(G)$ for every induced subgraph $H$ of $G$, and connected if $f(G)=\max(f(G_1),f(G_2))$ whenever $G$ is the disjoint union of $G_1$ and $G_2$. Following Dvořák and Norin, a colouring $\varphi$ of $G$ is $(f,p)$-proper if $f(G[\varphi^{-1}(c)])\le p$ for every colour $c$, and $\chi^\ell_{f,p}(G)$ is the least $s$ such that $G$ has an $(f,p)$-proper $L$-colouring for every list assignment $L$ with all lists of size at least $s$ (for $f=\Delta$ this is defective choosability, for $f$ the maximum component order it is clustered choosability). Following Esperet and Ochem, an $s$-island of $G$ is a non-empty set $I$ of vertices each having fewer than $s$ neighbours outside $I$, and $\mathrm{col}_{f,p}(G)$ is the least $s$ such that every induced subgraph $H$ of $G$ contains an $s$-island $I$ with $f(H[I])\le p$; for connected hereditary $f$ one has $\chi^\ell_{f,p}(G)\le\mathrm{col}_{f,p}(G)$, generalising $\chi^\ell(G)\le\mathrm{col}(G)$ for the ordinary colouring number. Alon proved that the colouring number is bounded by an exponential function of the choosability, and property (CC) asks for a weak converse of this kind for $f$. The authors show that $\mathrm{fan}$ (the maximum order of a fan, i.e. a path plus a vertex adjacent to all its vertices, contained as a subgraph) is monotone and connected but does not satisfy (CC). They give two sufficient conditions: a hereditary parameter satisfies the stronger property that $\chi^\ell_{f,p}(G)\le s$ bounds the ordinary colouring number if and only if $f$ bounds the average degree (which covers maximum degree, component size and treewidth); and (CC) holds when $f(G)$ is bounded by a function of $f(G[X])$ and $f(G-X)$ for all $X$, which covers the chromatic number. They were unable to fully describe the parameters satisfying (CC).
notes: Stated in prose without a labelled environment: 'While we were unable to fully describe the graph parameters satisfying (CC), we provide two sufficient conditions…'.
